orbit.title: Touch and Count
orbit.promptCompareSame: Count both groups. Do they have the same?
orbit.promptCompareMore: Count both groups. Which one has more?
orbit.promptScatter: Touch every {thing}. Do not miss any!
orbit.promptRow: Touch each {thing}. Count as you go!
orbit.printedCompare: Count both groups. Which has more?
orbit.methodCompare1: Count the first group and write the number down.
orbit.methodCompare3: The bigger number is the group with more — even if it takes up less room.
orbit.methodCount1: Count them one at a time, saying each number out loud.
orbit.methodCount2: Cross each one off as you count it, so none is counted twice.
orbit.methodCount3: The last number you say is how many there are.
orbit.hintCompareTip: Spreading things out does not make more.
orbit.hintCompareCounted: You have {a} on the left and {b} on the right. Finish both.
orbit.hintCompareStart: Touch the left group one at a time, then do the right.
orbit.hintCompareCounts: Left has {a}. Right has {b}. Which number is bigger?
orbit.hintScatterTip: Go in order so you do not miss any.
orbit.hintScatterStart: Start at the top and work down. Each {thing} keeps its number.
orbit.hintScatterGoing: {tapped} have numbers now. Touch a plain one and say "{next}".
orbit.hintScatterLastOne: One {thing} is still plain. Touch it and say "{word}".
orbit.hintScatterLeft: {left} {things} still need a number. Keep counting on to {count}.
orbit.hintRowTip: Say one number for each one you touch.
orbit.hintRowStart: Start at the far-left {thing}. Touch it and say "{word}".
orbit.hintRowGoing: You have counted {tapped}. Touch the next {thing} and say "{next}".
orbit.hintRowAll: Touch every {thing} in order. The last number, {count}, is how many.
orbit.finishScatter: Terrific tracking! You tagged all {count} scattered objects without missing any.
orbit.finishRow: You counted {count} {things}. The last number you said is how many!
orbit.compareSameRight: Both groups have {a}. Moving things around does not change how many!
orbit.compareLeftRight: The left group has {a}. The right group has {b}. Left has more!
orbit.compareRightRight: The right group has {b}. The left group has {a}. Right has more!
orbit.compareSameWrong: They look different, but count one by one. Left has {a} and right has {b}. The same!
orbit.compareWrong: Count one by one. Left has {a} {thingsA} and right has {b} {thingsB}.

subitize.title: Subitizing Rush
subitize.prompt: Look fast! How many did you see?
subitize.hintColorsTip: Count one colour, then keep going with the other.
subitize.hintColorsLook: Take in one colour as a group, then the other.
subitize.hintColorsParts: {a} of one colour, {b} of the other. Put them together.
subitize.hintPointsTip: Look for small groups inside the big group.
subitize.hintPointsLook: Do not chase every dot. Take in one clump, then count on.
subitize.hintPointsBunched: They were all bunched together. Split them into two smaller groups.
subitize.hintPointsSplit: {left} on the left and {right} on the right. Put them together.
subitize.hintGridTip: Try to see the pattern without counting.
subitize.hintGridLook: Look at the middle of the box, not at one dot.
subitize.hintGridShort: One short row of {total}. Read it like a domino.
subitize.hintGridOneRowMore: One row of three, and {spare} more underneath.
subitize.hintGridOneRow: One row of three and nothing else.
subitize.wrong: You said {choice}. There were {total}. Have another look!
subitize.howManyDots: How many dots did you see?

numberline.title: Froggy Skip
numberline.ruleDown: Pattern steps backward by -{step} each jump
numberline.ruleUp: Pattern steps forward by +{step} each jump
numberline.printedHop: Start at 0 and hop by {step} to reach {goal}. Write every number you land on.
numberline.methodMissing1: Look at the gap between two numbers you can see.
numberline.methodMissing2: That gap is the same all the way along.
numberline.methodMissing3: Count on — or back — from the number beside the hole.
numberline.methodHop1: Each hop is the same size: {step}.
numberline.methodHop2: Start at zero and add that much every time.
numberline.methodHop3: Write each number as you land on it — that is the count.
numberline.lineLabel: Number line with {pads} pads, hopping by {step}
numberline.hintMissingTip: Look at how much it grows each hop.
numberline.hintMissingSize: Every hop on this line is the same size. It goes {jump}.
numberline.hintMissingFrom: Start at {before} and go {jump}. That lands on the empty pad.
numberline.hintMissingBack: Go back {step} from {after} to reach the empty pad.
numberline.hintMissingCount: Count {jump} along the line until you reach the empty pad.
numberline.hintHopTip: Say the numbers out loud as you hop.
numberline.hintHopLast: The frog is on {here}, the last pad. That is your answer.
numberline.hintHopNext: The frog is on {here}. {here} + {step} is {next}. Press Hop.
numberline.hintHopChant: Chant the pads as you land: {pads}. The frog stops at {goal}.
numberline.hopDone: Ribbit! The frog leaped by +{step} each pad all the way to {goal}!
numberline.missingWrong: Look at the jump between neighboring pads to find the missing number.

tenframe.title: Ten-Frame Rocket
tenframe.promptComplement: You have {initial}. How many more to make 10?
tenframe.promptTeen: Make {target}. Fill one frame with 10, then add more.
tenframe.promptFill: Make {target} dots. Fill the top row first.
tenframe.printedComplement: The frame holds {initial}. How many more make 10?
tenframe.printedTeen: Draw {target}. Fill one frame with ten, then start the next.
tenframe.printedFill: Draw {target} dots. Fill the top row first.
tenframe.printedFillAnswerBelow: {target} — {top} on the top row and {below} below
tenframe.methodComplement2: Count the empty cells rather than the full ones.
tenframe.methodComplement3: That is how many more you need.
tenframe.methodTeen1: A teen number is a full ten and some ones.
tenframe.methodTeen2: Fill one frame completely, then put the rest in the next.
tenframe.methodTeen3: The full frame is the ten you do not need to count again.
tenframe.methodFill1: Fill the top row first — a full row is five.
tenframe.methodFill2: Put the rest in the bottom row.
tenframe.methodFill3: A full row is seen without counting, which is the point of the frame.
tenframe.hintComplementTip: Count the empty boxes. That is how many more.

hintComplementFull.one: {count} box is full. A full frame is 10.
hintComplementFull.other: {count} boxes are full. A full frame is 10.

tenframe.hintComplementCount: Count the empty boxes one at a time, then tap that number.
tenframe.hintTeenTip: One full frame is 10. Then count the extra ones.
tenframe.hintTeenSplit: {target} is 10 and {ones} more. Put {ones} in the second frame.
tenframe.hintTeenLess: You have 10 and {filled}. Take {less} back out.
tenframe.hintFillTip: Fill the top row to 5 first. That makes it easy!
tenframe.hintFillFits: {target} fits in the top row. Fill {target} and stop.
tenframe.hintFillSplit: {target} is a full top row of 5, and {extra} more below.
tenframe.hintFillStart: Tap {target} boxes, top row first, then press Check.
tenframe.hintFillMore: You have {filled}. Tap {more} more, then press Check.
tenframe.hintFillLess: You have {filled}. Tap {less} off, then press Check.
tenframe.cellFilledNext: Space {position}, filled, fill this one next
tenframe.cellEmptyNext: Space {position}, empty, fill this one next
tenframe.fillRight: Rocket fueled! You filled 5 on top plus {extra} extra ones to make {target}.
tenframe.fillWrong: Currently filled: {filled}. We need exactly {target} filled spots.
tenframe.complementRight: Number bond discovered! {initial} + {guess} = 10. You completed the full ten-frame.
tenframe.complementWrong: There are {initial} filled spots. Count the empty ones: we need {target} more to make 10.
tenframe.teenWrong: Currently 10 + {filled} = {built}. We need {ones} extra ones in Frame 2.
tenframe.selectEmpty: Select how many empty spots are needed to make 10:

base10.title: Base-10 Foundry
base10.prompt: Make {target} out of tens and ones.
base10.printedHundreds: Draw {target} using hundreds, tens and ones.
base10.methodHundreds1: Take as many whole hundreds as you can.
base10.methodHundreds2: Then as many whole tens from what is left.
base10.methodHundreds3: Whatever remains is the ones. Ten tens make a hundred — never leave ten loose tens.
base10.methodTens1: Take as many whole tens as you can.
base10.methodTens2: Whatever is left over is the ones.
base10.methodTens3: Ten ones make one ten — never leave ten loose ones behind.
base10.hintTip: Use the big blocks first, then the small ones.
base10.hintBundleOnes: You have {ones} ones. Ten of them make one ten — press "Make a Ten".
base10.hintBundleTens: You have {tens} tens. Ten of them make one hundred — press "Make a Hundred".
base10.hintReady: The columns hold {places}. That is {target}. Press Check.
base10.hintTooMany: You have {value}, which is {over} too many. Drag some back out.
base10.wrongTotal: Your current total is {value} blocks, but you need to build exactly {target}.
base10.groupOnesMsg: Great total! But you have {ones} Ones. Put 10 of them together to make a Ten.
base10.groupTensMsg: Great total! But you have {tens} Tens. Put 10 of them together to make a Hundred.
base10.spokenAdd: Add more blocks to make the number.
base10.dragHint: Drag a block into its column
